summary: Full-stack E2E validation of Batch Document Queue + Batch Audit Summary feature set. Backend: 48/48 pytest cases PASS (6 dedicated batch tests: single-doc flow, mixed PDF+DOCX with distinct profiles, partial failure isolation with fail-closed batch status, cancellation cleanup, zip-slip/path-traversal protection, concurrency semaphore enforcement). Frontend: full batch UI flow validated end-to-end on preview URL: mode toggle -> multi-upload (PDF+DOCX) -> per-doc profile/remove controls -> start analysis -> both docs progress to 'Revisión requerida' with match counts (11 for PDF, 14 for DOCX) -> review canvas per doc with accept-all + next/prev batch nav + back-to-queue -> batch purge (both -> Verificado) -> ZIP/audit(PDF)/audit(JSON) buttons all enabled. Single-mode regression verified after toggling back. Fail-closed behavior fully covered at backend layer (test_batch_partial_failure_and_isolation asserts completed_with_errors, ZIP excludes corrupt doc, summary metrics correct).
critical_code_review_comments: batch.py compute_batch_status is well-structured: strict fail-closed logic — completed_verified requires ALL docs verified; any error/cancelled/verification_failed => completed_with_errors. Test coverage confirms it.

build_batch_zip correctly enforces sovereignty: only doc.status=='verified' entries added under documents/; audits are always emitted. Arcnames use os.path.basename to defeat zip-slip. Verified by test_batch_zip_slip_and_path_traversal_protection.
generate_batch_audit_summary aggregates ONLY metadata + sha256 hashes + counts, no plaintext PII by construction. Safe.

Semaphore per batch caps concurrency via BATCH_MAX_CONCURRENT_DOCUMENTS env; get_semaphore(batch_id) lazily initializes. Suggestion (non-blocking): purge existing semaphore in cleanup_batch to avoid unbounded map growth over long-lived processes.
App.js still contains 'http://localhost:8001' fallback for REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL — carry-over from prior iterations; violates fail-fast env policy but out of scope for this review.

BatchQueueScreen exposes all required data-testids (toggle-batch-mode-btn, batch-dropzone, batch-file-input, start-batch-analysis-btn, batch-purge-ready-btn, batch-download-zip-btn, batch-audit-pdf-btn, batch-audit-json-btn, batch-filter-status, doc-profile-select-*, cancel-doc-btn-*, remove-doc-btn-*, review-doc-btn-*, batch-doc-row-*). Review canvas exposes batch-prev-doc-btn, batch-next-doc-btn, back-to-batch-queue-btn, accept-all-matches-btn. Test-friendly.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (batch E2E: upload -> analyze -> review nav -> purge -> ZIP/audit + single-mode regression)

seed_data_creation: Batch created in-browser via multi-upload of /app/backend/fixtures/sample_rrhh_payroll.pdf + /app/backend/fixtures/sample_legal_contract.docx; auto-cleaned on session TTL.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Regression command: `cd /app && PYTHONPATH=/app python -m pytest backend/tests/ -v` (48 tests, ~52s). For UI batch tests use state='attached' when calling set_input_files on [data-testid='batch-file-input'] since it is a hidden native input. Backend fixtures in /app/backend/fixtures. All batch data-testids follow patterns doc-profile-select-{id}, cancel-doc-btn-{id}, remove-doc-btn-{id}, review-doc-btn-{id}, batch-doc-row-{id}.
rca of the issue: No product-level bugs found. Only tooling nuance: Playwright wait_for_selector defaults to state='visible' which fails on the intentionally hidden multi-file input; using state='attached' resolves it.
